sections.t: Wrongful gain
sections.b:
“Wrongful gain”: Wrongful gain is gain by unlawful means of property to which the person gaining is not legally entitled.
“Wrongful loss”: Wrongful loss is the loss by unlawful means of property to which the person losing it is legally entitled.
“Gaining wrongfully”: A person is said to gain wrongfully when such person retains wrongfully, as well as when such person acquires wrongfully.
“Losing wrongfully”: A person is said to lose wrongfully when such person is wrongfully kept out of any property, as well as when such person is wrongfully deprived of property.

sections.t: Construction of reference to transportation
sections.b:
Subject to the provisions of sub-section (2) and sub-section (3), any reference to “transportation for life” in any other law for the time being in force or in any instrument or order having effect by virtue of any such law or of any enactment repealed shall be construed as a reference to “imprisonment for life”. In every case in which a sentence of transportation for a term has been passed before the commencement of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Act, 1955, (26 of 1955), the offender shall be dealt with in the same manner as if sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for the same term. Any reference to transportation for a term or to transportation for any shorter term (by whatever name called) in any other law for the time being in force shall be deemed to have been omitted.
Any reference to “transportation” in any other law for the time being in force shall
if the expression means transportation for life, be construed as a reference to imprisonment for life;
if the expression means transportation for any shorter term, be deemed to have been omitted.

sections.t: Imprisonment for non-payment of fine, when offence punishable with fine only
sections.b:
If the offence be punishable with fine only, the imprisonment which the Court imposes in default of payment of the fine shall be simple, and the term for which the Court directs the offender to be imprisoned, in default of payment of fine, shall not exceed the following scale, that is to say,
for any term not exceeding two months when the amount of the fine shall not exceed fifty rupees,
and for any term not exceeding four months when the amount shall not exceed one hundred rupees,
and for any term not exceeding six months in any other case.

x.targetTitle: Amount of fine, liability in default of payment of fine, etc
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 67 'Imprisonment for non-payment of fine, when offence punishable with fine only' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 8(5) 'Amount of fine, liability in default of payment of fine, etc' under CHAPTER II OF PUNISHMENTS with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Imprisonment to terminate on payment of fine
sections.b: The imprisonment which is imposed in default of payment of a fine shall terminate whenever that fine is either paid or levied by process of law.

x.targetTitle: Amount of fine, liability in default of payment of fine, etc
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 68 'Imprisonment to terminate on payment of fine' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 8(6)(a) 'Amount of fine, liability in default of payment of fine, etc' under CHAPTER II OF PUNISHMENTS.

sections.t: Termination of imprisonment on payment of proportional part of fine
sections.b: If, before the expiration of the term of imprisonment fixed in default of payment, such a proportion of the fine be paid or levied that the term of imprisonment suffered in default of payment is not less than proportional to the part of the fine still unpaid, the imprisonment shall terminate.

x.targetTitle: Amount of fine, liability in default of payment of fine, etc
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 69 'Termination of imprisonment on payment of proportional part of fine' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 8(6)(b) 'Amount of fine, liability in default of payment of fine, etc' under CHAPTER II OF PUNISHMENTS.

sections.t: Fine leviable within six years, or during imprisonment. Death not to discharge property from liability
sections.b:
The fine, or any part thereof which remains unpaid, may be levied at any time within six years after the passing of the sentence, and if, under the sentence, the offender be liable to imprisonment for a longer period than six years, then at any time previous to the expiration of that period;
and the death of the offender does not discharge from the liability any property which would, after his death, be legally liable for his debts.

x.targetTitle: Amount of fine, liability in default of payment of fine, etc
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 70 'Fine leviable within six years, of during imprisonment. Death not to discharge property from liability' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 8(7) 'Amount of fine, liability in default of payment of fine, etc' under CHAPTER II OF PUNISHMENTS.

sections.t: Limit of punishment of offence made up of several offences
sections.b: Where anything which is an offence is made up of parts, any of which parts is itself an offence, the offender shall not be punished with the punishment of more than one of such his offences, unless it be so expressly provided.

x.targetTitle: Limit of punishment of offence made up of several offences
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 71 'Limit of punishment of offence made up of several offences' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 9 'Limit of punishment of offence made up of several offences' under CHAPTER II OF PUNISHMENTS.

sections.t: Punishment of person guilty of one of several offences, the judgment stating that it is doubtful of which
sections.b: In all cases in which judgment is given that a person is guilty of one of several offences specified in the judgment, but that it is doubtful of which of these offences he is guilty, the offender shall be punished for the offence for which the lowest punishment is provided if the same punishment is not provided for all.

x.targetTitle: Punishment of person guilty of one of several offences, judgment stating that it is doubtful of which
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 72 'Punishment of person guilty of one of several offences, the judgment stating that it is doubtful of which' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 10 'Punishment of person guilty of one of several offences, judgment stating that it is doubtful of which' under CHAPTER II OF PUNISHMENTS.

sections.t: Solitary confinement

x.targetTitle: Solitary confinement
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 73 'Solitary confinement' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 11 'Solitary confinement' under CHAPTER II OF PUNISHMENTS.

sections.t: Limit of solitary confinement
sections.b:
In executing a sentence of solitary confinement, such confinement shall in no case exceed fourteen days at a time, with intervals between the periods of solitary confinement of not less duration than such periods;
and when the imprisonment awarded shall exceed three months, the solitary confinement shall not exceed seven days in any one month of the whole imprisonment awarded, with intervals between the periods of solitary confinement of not less duration than such periods.

x.targetTitle: Limit of solitary confinement
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 74 'Limit of solitary confinement' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 12 'Limit of solitary confinement' under CHAPTER II OF PUNISHMENTS.

sections.t: Enhanced punishment for certain offences under Chapter XII or Chapter XVII after previous conviction
sections.b: Whoever, having been convicted: by a Court in India, of an offence punishable under Chapter XII or Chapter XVII of this Code with imprisonment of either description for a term of three years or upwards, shall be guilty of any offence punishable under either of those Chapters with like imprisonment for the like term, shall be subject for every such subsequent offence to imprisonment for life or to imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years.

x.targetTitle: Enhanced punishment for certain offences after previous conviction
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 75 'Enhanced punishment for certain offences under Chapter XII or Chapter XVII after previous conviction' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 13 'Enhanced punishment for certain offences after previous conviction' under CHAPTER II OF PUNISHMENTS.

sections.t: Act done by a person bound, or by mistake of fact believing himself bound, by law
sections.b: Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who is, or who by reason of a mistake of fact and not by reason of a mistake of law in good faith believes himself to be, bound by law to do it.

x.targetTitle: Act done by a person bound, or by mistake of fact believing himself bound, by law
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 76 'Act done by a person bound, or by mistake of fact believing himself bound, by law' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 14 'Act done by a person bound, or by mistake of fact believing himself bound, by law' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Act of Judge when acting judicially
sections.b: Nothing is an offence which is done by a Judge when acting judicially in the exercise of any power which is, or which in good faith he believes to be, given to him by law.

x.targetTitle: Act of Judge when acting judicially
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 77 'Act of Judge when acting judicially' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 15 'Act of Judge when acting judicially' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Act done pursuant to the judgment or order of Court
sections.b: Nothing which is done in pursuance of, or which is warranted by the judgment or order of, a Court of Justice, if done whilst such judgment or order remains in force, is an offence, notwithstanding the Court may have had no jurisdiction to pass such judgment or order, provided the person doing the act in good faith believes that the Court had such jurisdiction.

x.targetTitle: Act done pursuant to judgment or order of Court
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 78 'Act done pursuant to the judgment or order of Court' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 16 'Act done pursuant to judgment or order of Court' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Act done by a person justified, or by mistake of fact believing himself, justified, by law
sections.b: Nothing is an offence which is done by any person who is justified by law, or who by reason of a mistake of fact and not by reason of a mistake of law in good faith, believes himself to be justified by law, in doing it.

x.targetTitle: Act done by a person justified, or by mistake of fact believing himself justified, by law
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 79 'Act done by a person justified, or by mistake of fact believing himself, justified, by law' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 17 'Act done by a person justified, or by mistake of fact believing himself justified, by law' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Accident in doing a lawful act
sections.b: Nothing is an offence which is done by accident or misfortune, and without any criminal intention or knowledge in the doing of a lawful act in a lawful manner by lawful means and with proper care and caution.

x.targetTitle: Accident in doing a lawful act
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 80 'Accident in doing a lawful act' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 18 'Accident in doing a lawful act' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Act likely to cause harm, but done without criminal intent, and to prevent other harm
sections.b: Nothing is an offence merely by reason of its being done with the knowledge that it is likely to cause harm, if it be done without any criminal intention to cause harm, and in good faith for the purpose of preventing or avoiding other harm to person or property.

x.targetTitle: Act likely to cause harm, but done without criminal intent, and to prevent other harm
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 81 'Act likely to cause harm, but done without criminal intent, and to prevent other harm' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 19 'Act likely to cause harm, but done without criminal intent, and to prevent other harm' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Act of a child under seven years of age
sections.b: Nothing is an offence which is done by a child under seven years of age.

x.targetTitle: Act of a child under seven years of age
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 82 'Act of a child under seven years of age' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 20 'Act of a child under seven years of age' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Act of a child above seven and under twelve of immature understanding
sections.b: Nothing is an offence which is done by a child above seven years of age and under twelve, who has not attained sufficient maturity or understanding to judge the nature and consequences of his conduct on that occasion.

x.targetTitle: Act of a child above seven and under twelve years of age of immature understanding
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 83 'Act of a child above seven and under twelve of immature understanding' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 21 'Act of a child above seven and under twelve years of age of immature understanding' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Act of a person of unsound mind
sections.b: Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who, at the time of doing it, by reason of unsoundness of mind, is incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or that he is doing what is either wrong or contrary to law.

x.targetTitle: Act of a person of unsound mind
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 84 'Act of a person of unsound mind' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 22 'Act of a person of unsound mind' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Act of a person incapable of judgment by reason of intoxication caused against his will
sections.b:
Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who, at the time of doing it, is, by reason of intoxication, incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or that he is doing what is either wrong, or contrary to law:
Provided that the thing which intoxicated him was administered to him without his knowledge or against his will.

x.targetTitle: Act of a person incapable of judgment by reason of intoxication caused against his will
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 85 'Act of a person incapable of judgment by reason of intoxication caused against his will' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 23 'Act of a person incapable of judgment by reason of intoxication caused against his will' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Offence requiring a particular intent or knowledge committed by one who is intoxicated
sections.b: In cases where an act done is not an offence unless done with a particular knowledge or intent, a person who does the act in a state of intoxication shall be liable to be dealt with as if he had the same knowledge as he would have had if he had not been intoxicated, unless the thing which intoxicated him was administered to him without his knowledge or against his will.

x.targetTitle: Offence requiring a particular intent or knowledge committed by one who is intoxicated
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 86 'Offence requiring a particular intent or knowledge committed by one who is intoxicated' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 24 'Offence requiring a particular intent or knowledge committed by one who is intoxicated' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Act not intended and not known to be likely to cause death or grievous hurt, done by consent
sections.b:
Nothing which is not intended to cause death, or grievous hurt, and which is not known by the doer to be likely to cause death or grievous hurt, is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause, or be intended by the doer to cause, to any person, above eighteen years of age, who has given consent, whether express or implied, to suffer that harm;
Or by reason of any harm which it may be known by the doer to be likely to cause to any such person who has consented to take the risk of that harm.

x.targetTitle: Act not intended and not known to be likely to cause death or grievous hurt, done by consent
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 87 'Act not intended and not known to be likely to cause death or grievous hurt, done by consent' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 25 'Act not intended and not known to be likely to cause death or grievous hurt, done by consent' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Act not intended to cause death, done by consent in good faith for person's benefit
sections.b: Nothing, which is not intended to cause death, is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause, or be intended by the doer to cause, or be known by the doer to be likely to cause, to any person for whose benefit it is done in good faith, and who has given a consent, whether express or implied to suffer that harm, or to take the risk of that harm.

x.targetTitle: Act not intended to cause death, done by consent in good faith for person's benefit
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 88 'Act not intended to cause death, done by consent in good faith for person's benefit' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 26 'Act not intended to cause death, done by consent in good faith for person's benefit' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Act done in good faith for benefit of child or insane person, by or by consent of guardian
sections.b: Nothing which is done in good faith for the benefit of a person under twelve years of age, or of unsound mind, by or by consent, either express or implied, of the guardian or other person having lawful charge of that person, is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause, or be intended by the doer to cause or be known by the doer to be likely to cause to that person; Provided:

x.targetTitle: Act done in good faith for benefit of child or person of unsound mind, by or by consent of guardian
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 89 'Act done in good faith for benefit of child or insane person, by or by consent of guardian' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 27 'Act done in good faith for benefit of child or person of unsound mind, by or by consent of guardian' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Consent known to be given under fear or misconception
sections.b:
A consent is not such a consent as is intended by any section of this Code, if the consent is given by a person under fear of injury, or under a misconception of fact, and if the person doing the act knows, or has reason to believe, that the consent was given in consequence of such fear or misconception; or
Consent of insane person if the consent is given by a person who, from unsoundness of mind, or intoxication, is unable to understand the nature and consequence of that to which he gives his consent; or
Consent of child unless the contrary appears from the context, if the consent is given by a person who is under twelve years of age.

x.targetTitle: Consent known to be given under fear or misconception
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 90 'Consent known to be given under fear or misconception' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 28 'Consent known to be given under fear or misconception' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Exclusion of acts which are offences independently of harm cause
sections.b: The exceptions in sections 87, 88 and 89 do not extend to acts which are offences independently of any harm which they may cause, or be intended to cause, or be known to be likely to cause, to the person giving the consent, or on whose behalf the consent is given.

x.targetTitle: Exclusion of acts which are offences independently of harm caused
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 91 'Exclusion of acts which are offences independently of harm caused' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 29 'Exclusion of acts which are offences independently of harm caused' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Act done in good faith for benefit of a person without consent
sections.b: Nothing is an offence by reason of any harm which it may causes to a person for whose benefit it is done in good faith, even without that person’s consent, if the circumstances are such that it is impossible for that person to signify consent, or if that person is incapable of giving consent, and has no guardian or other person in lawful charge of him from whom it is possible to obtain consent in time for the thing to be done with benefit;

x.targetTitle: Act done in good faith for benefit of a person without consent
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 92 'Act done in good faith for benefit of a person without consent' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 30 'Act done in good faith for benefit of a person without consent' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Communication made in good faith
sections.b: No communication made in good faith is an offence by reason of any harm to the person to whom it is made, if it is made for the benefit of that person.

x.targetTitle: Communication made in good faith
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 93 'Communication made in good faith' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 31 'Communication made in good faith' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Act to which a person is compelled by threats
sections.b: Except murder, and offences against the State punishable with death, nothing is an offence which is done by a person who is compelled to do it by threats, which, at the time of doing it, reasonably cause the apprehension that instant death to that person will otherwise be the consequence;

x.targetTitle: Act to which a person is compelled by threats
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 94 'Act to which a person is compelled by threats' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 32 'Act to which a person is compelled by threats' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Act causing slight harm
sections.b: Nothing is an offence by reason that it causes, or that it is intended to cause, or that it is known to be likely to cause, any harm, if that harm is so slight that no person of ordinary sense and temper would complain of such harm.

x.targetTitle: Act causing slight harm
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 95 'Act causing slight harm' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 33 'Act causing slight harm' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Things done in private defence
sections.b: Nothing is an offence which is done in the exercise of the right of private defence.

x.targetTitle: Things done in private defence
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 96 'Things done in private defence' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 34 'Things done in private defence' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Right of private defence of the body and of property
sections.b:
Every person has a right, subject to the restrictions contained in section 99, to defend: His own body, and the body of any other person, against any offence affecting the human body;
The property, whether movable or immovable, of himself or of any other person, against any act which is an offence falling under the definition of theft, robbery, mischief or criminal trespass, or which is an attempt to commit theft, robbery, mischief or criminal trespass.

x.targetTitle: Right of private defence of body and of property
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 97 'Right of private defence of the body and of property' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 35 'Right of private defence of body and of property' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Right of private defence against the act of a person of unsound mind, etc.
sections.b: When an act which would otherwise be a certain offence, is not that offence, by reason of the youth, the want of maturity of understanding, the unsoundness of mind or the intoxication of the person doing that act, or by reason of any misconception on the part of that person, every person has the same right of private defence against that act which he would have if the act were that offence.

x.targetTitle: Right of private defence against act of a person of unsound mind, etc
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 98 'Right of private defence against the act of a person of unsound mind, etc' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 36 'Right of private defence against act of a person of unsound mind, etc' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Acts against which there is no right of private defence
sections.b: There is no right of private defence against an act which does not reasonably cause the apprehension of death or of grievous hurt, if done, or attempted to be done, by a public servant acting in good faith under colour of his office, though that act may not be strictly justifiable by law.

x.targetTitle: Acts against which there is no right of private defence
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 99 'Acts against which there is no right of private defence' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 37 'Acts against which there is no right of private defence' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: When the right of private defence of the body extends to causing death
sections.b: The right of private defence of the body extends, under the restrictions mentioned in the last preceding section, to the voluntary causing of death or of any other harm to the assailant, if the offence which occasions the exercise of the right be of any of the descriptions hereinafter enumerated, namely:

x.targetTitle: When right of private defence of body extends to causing death
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 100 'When the right of private defence of the body extends to causing death' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 38 'When right of private defence of body extends to causing death' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: When such right extends to causing any harm other than death
sections.b: If the offence be not of any of the descriptions enumerated in the last preceding section, the right of private defence of the body does not extend to the voluntary causing of death to the assailant, but does extend, under the restrictions mentioned in section 99, to the voluntary causing to the assailant of any harm other than death.

x.targetTitle: When such right extends to causing any harm other than death
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 101 'When such right extends to causing any harm other than death' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 39 'When such right extends to causing any harm other than death' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Commencement and continuance of the right of private defence of the body
sections.b: The right of private defence of the body commences as soon as a reasonable apprehension of danger to the body arises from an attempt or threat to commit the offence though the offence may not have been committed; and it continues as long as such apprehension of danger to the body continues.

x.targetTitle: Commencement and continuance of right of private defence of body
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 102 'Commencement and continuance of the right of private defence of the body' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 40 'Commencement and continuance of right of private defence of body' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: When the right of private defence of property extends to causing death
sections.b: The right of private defence of property extends, under the restrictions mentioned in section 99, to the voluntary causing of death or of any other harm to the wrong-doer, if the offence, the committing of which, or the attempting to commit which, occasions the exercise of the right, be an offence of any of the descriptions hereinafter enumerated, namely:

x.targetTitle: When right of private defence of property extends to causing death
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 103 'When the right of private defence of property extends to causing death' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 41 'When right of private defence of property extends to causing death' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: When such right to causing any harm other than death
sections.b: If the offence, the committing of which, or the attempting to commit which occasions the exercise of the right of private defence, be theft, mischief, or criminal trespass, not of any of the descriptions enumerated in the last preceding section, that right does not extend to the voluntary causing of death, but does extend, subject to the restrictions mentioned in section 99, to the voluntary causing to the wrong-doer of any harm other than death.

x.targetTitle: When such right extends to causing any harm other than death
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 104 'When such right extends to causing any harm other than death' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 42 'When such right extends to causing any harm other than death' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Commencement and continuance of the right of private defence of property
sections.b: The right of private defence of property commences when a reasonable apprehension of danger to the property commences.

x.targetTitle: Commencement and continuance of right of private defence of property
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 105 'Commencement and continuance of the right of private defence of property' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 43 'Commencement and continuance of right of private defence of property' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Right of private defence against deadly assault when there is risk of harm to innocent person
sections.b: If in the exercise of the right of private defence against an assault which reasonably causes the apprehension of death, the defender be so situated that he cannot effectually exercise that right without risk of harm to an innocent person, his right of private defence extends to the running of that risk.

x.targetTitle: Right of private defence against deadly assault when there is risk of harm to innocent person
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 106 'Right of private defence against deadly assault when there is risk of harm to innocent person' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 44 'Right of private defence against deadly assault when there is risk of harm to innocent person' under CHAPTER III GENERAL EXCEPTIONS.

sections.t: Abetment of a thing
sections.b:
A person abets the doing of a thing, who: Instigates any person to do that thing; or
Engages with one or more other person or persons in any conspiracy for the doing of that thing, if an act or illegal omission takes place in pursuance of that conspiracy, and in order to the doing of that thing; or
Intentionally aids, by any act or illegal omission, the doing of that thing.

x.targetTitle: Abetment of a thing
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 107 'Abetment of a thing' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 45 'Abetment of a thing' under CHAPTER IV OF ABETMENT, CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY AND ATTEMPT.

sections.t: Abettor
sections.b: A person abets an offence, who abets either the commission of an offence, or the commission of an act which would be an offence, if committed by a person capable by law of committing an offence with the same intention or knowledge as that of the abettor.

x.targetTitle: Abettor
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 108 'Abettor' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 46 'Abettor' under CHAPTER IV OF ABETMENT, CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY AND ATTEMPT.

sections.t: Abetment in India of offences outside India
sections.b: A person abets an offence within the meaning of this Code who, in India, abets the commission of any act without and beyond India which would constitute an offence if committed in India.

x.targetTitle: Abetment in India of offences outside India
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 108A 'Abetment in India of offences outside India' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 47 'Abetment in India of offences outside India' under CHAPTER IV OF ABETMENT, CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY AND ATTEMPT.

sections.t: Punishment of abetment if the act abetted is committed in consequence and where no express provision is made for its punishment
sections.b: Whoever abets any offence shall, if the act abetted is committed in consequence of the abetment, and no express provision is made by this Code for the punishment of such abetment, be punished with the punishment provided for the offence.

x.targetTitle: Punishment of abetment if act abetted is committed in consequence and where no express provision is made for its punishment
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 109 'Punishment of abetment if the act abetted is committed in consequence and where no express provision is made for its punishment' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 49 'Punishment of abetment if act abetted is committed in consequence and where no express provision is made for its punishment' under CHAPTER IV OF ABETMENT, CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY AND ATTEMPT.

sections.t: Punishment of abetment if person abetted does act with different intention from that of abettor
sections.b: Whoever abets the commission of an offence shall, if the person abetted does the act with a different intention or knowledge from that of the abettor, be punished with the punishment provided for the offence which would have been committed if the act had been done with the intention or knowledge of the abettor and with no other.

x.targetTitle: Punishment of abetment if person abetted does act with different intention from that of abettor
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 110 'Punishment of abetment if person abetted does act with different intention from that of abettor' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 50 'Punishment of abetment if person abetted does act with different intention from that of abettor' under CHAPTER IV OF ABETMENT, CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY AND ATTEMPT.

sections.t: Liability of abettor when one act abetted and different act done
sections.b: When an Act is abetted and a different act is done, the abettor is liable for the act done, in the same manner and to the same extent as if he had directly abetted it.

x.targetTitle: Liability of abettor when one act abetted and different act done
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 111 'Liability of abettor when one act abetted and different act done' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 51 'Liability of abettor when one act abetted and different act done' under CHAPTER IV OF ABETMENT, CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY AND ATTEMPT.

sections.t: Abettor when liable to cumulative punishment for act abetted and for act done
sections.b: If the act for which the abettor is liable under the last preceding section is committed in addition to the act abetted, and constitute a distinct offence, the abettor is liable to punishment for each of the offences.

x.targetTitle: Abettor when liable to cumulative punishment for act abetted and for act done
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 112 'Abettor when liable to cumulative punishment for act abetted and for act done' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 52 'Abettor when liable to cumulative punishment for act abetted and for act done' under CHAPTER IV OF ABETMENT, CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY AND ATTEMPT.

sections.t: Liability of abettor for an effect caused by the act abetted different from that intended by the abettor
sections.b: When an act is abetted with the intention on the part of the abettor of causing a particular effect, and an act for which the abettor is liable in consequence of the abetment, causes a different effect from that intended by the abettor, the abettor is liable for the effect caused, in the same manner and to the same extent as if he had abetted the act with the intention of causing that effect, provided he knew that the act abetted was likely to cause that effect.

x.targetTitle: Liability of abettor for an effect caused by act abetted different from that intended by abettor
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 113 'Liability of abettor for an effect caused by the act abetted different from that intended by the abettor' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 53 'Liability of abettor for an effect caused by act abetted different from that intended by abettor' under CHAPTER IV OF ABETMENT, CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY AND ATTEMPT.

sections.t: Abettor present when offence is committed
sections.b: Whenever any person who if absent would be liable to be punished as an abettor, is present when the act or offence for which he would be punishable in consequence of the abetment is committed, he shall be deemed to have committed such act or offence.

x.targetTitle: Abettor present when offence is committed
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 114 'Abettor present when offence is committed' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 54 'Abettor present when offence is committed' under CHAPTER IV OF ABETMENT, CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY AND ATTEMPT.

sections.t: Abetment of offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life if offence not committed
sections.b: Whoever abets the commission of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, shall, if that offence be not committed in consequence of the abetment, and no express provision is made by this Code for the punishment of such abetment, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine;

x.targetTitle: Abetment of offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 115 'Abetment of offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life.-if offence not committed' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 55 'Abetment of offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life' under CHAPTER IV OF ABETMENT, CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY AND ATTEMPT.

sections.t: Abetment of offence punishable with imprisonment -- if offence be not committed
sections.b:
Whoever abets an offence punishable with imprisonment shall, if that offence be not committed in consequence of the abetment, and no express provision is made by this Code for the punishment of such abetment, be punished with imprisonment of any description provided for that offence for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term provided for that offence;
or with such fine as is provided for that offence, or with both;

x.targetTitle: Abetment of offence punishable with imprisonment
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 116 'Abetment of offence punishable with imprisonment-if offence be not committed' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 56 'Abetment of offence punishable with imprisonment' under CHAPTER IV OF ABETMENT, CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY AND ATTEMPT.

sections.t: Abetting commission of offence by the public or by more than ten persons
sections.b: Whoever abets the commission of an offence by the public generally or by any number or class of persons exceeding ten, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Abetting commission of offence by public or by more than ten persons
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 117 'Abetting commission of offence by the public or by more than ten persons' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 57 'Abetting commission of offence by public or by more than ten persons' under CHAPTER IV OF ABETMENT, CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY AND ATTEMPT with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life
sections.b: Whoever intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, voluntarily conceals, by any act or illegal omission, the existence of a design to commit such offence or makes any representation which he knows to be false respecting such design:

x.targetTitle: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 118 'Concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 58 'Concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life' under CHAPTER IV OF ABETMENT, CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY AND ATTEMPT.

sections.t: Public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent
sections.b: Whoever, being a public servant intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence which it is his duty as such public servant to prevent, voluntarily conceals, by any act or illegal omission, the existence of a design to commit such offence, or makes any representation which he knows to be false respecting such design:

x.targetTitle: Public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 119 'Public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 59 'Public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent' under CHAPTER IV OF ABETMENT, CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY AND ATTEMPT.

sections.t: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with imprisonment
sections.b: Whoever, intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence punishable with imprisonment, voluntarily conceals, by any act or illegal omission, the existence of a design to commit such offence, or makes any representation which he knows to be false respecting such design:

x.targetTitle: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with imprisonment
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 120 'Concealing design to commit offence punishable with imprisonment' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 60 'Concealing design to commit offence punishable with imprisonment' under CHAPTER IV OF ABETMENT, CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY AND ATTEMPT.

sections.t: Definition of criminal conspiracy
sections.b:
When two or more persons agree to do, or cause to be done:
an illegal act, or
an act which is not illegal by illegal means, such an agreement is designated a criminal conspiracy;
Provided that no agreement except an agreement to commit an offence shall amount to a criminal conspiracy unless some act besides the agreement is done by one or more parties to such agreement in pursuance thereof.

x.targetTitle: Criminal conspiracy
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 120A 'Definition of criminal conspiracy' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 61(1) 'Criminal conspiracy' under CHAPTER IV OF ABETMENT, CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY AND ATTEMPT.

sections.t: Punishment of criminal conspiracy
sections.b:
Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable with death, imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment for a term of two years or upwards, shall, where no express provision is made in this Code for the punishment of such a conspiracy, be punished in the same manner as if he had abetted such offence.
Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy other than a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable as aforesaid shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding six months, or with fine or with both.

x.targetTitle: Criminal conspiracy
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 120B 'Punishment of criminal conspiracy' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 61(2) 'Criminal conspiracy' under CHAPTER IV OF ABETMENT, CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY AND ATTEMPT.

sections.t: Waging, or attempting to wage war, or abetting waging of war, against the Government of India
sections.b: Whoever wages war against the Government of India, or attempts to wage such war, or abets the waging of such war, shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Waging, or attempting to wage war, or abetting waging of war, against Government of India
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 121 'Waging, or attempting to wage war, or abetting waging of war, against the Government of India' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 147 'Waging, or attempting to wage war, or abetting waging of war, against Government of India' under CHAPTER VII OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE STATE.

sections.t: Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 121
sections.b: Whoever within or without India conspires to commit any of the offences punishable by section 121, or conspires to overawe, by means of criminal force or the show of criminal force, the Central Government or any State Government, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 147
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 121A 'Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 121' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 148 'Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 147' under CHAPTER VII OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE STATE.

sections.t: Collecting arms, etc., with intention of waging war against the Government of India
sections.b: Whoever collects men, arms or ammunition or otherwise prepares to wage war with the intention of either waging or being prepared to wage war against the Government of India, shall be punished with imprisonment for life or imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Collecting arms, etc., with intention of waging war against Government of India
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 122 'Collecting arms, etc., with intention of waging war against the Government of India' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 149 'Collecting arms, etc., with intention of waging war against Government of India' under CHAPTER VII OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE STATE.

sections.t: Concealing with intent to facilitate design to wage war
sections.b: Whoever, by any act, or by any illegal omission, conceals the existence of a design to wage war against the Government of India, intending by such concealment to facilitate, or knowing it to be likely that such concealment will facilitate, the waging of such war, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Concealing with intent to facilitate design to wage war
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 123 'Concealing with intent to facilitate design to wage war' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 150 'Concealing with intent to facilitate design to wage war' under CHAPTER VII OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE STATE.

sections.t: Assaulting President, Governor, etc., with intent to compel or restrain the exercise of any lawful power
sections.b: Whoever, with the intention of inducing or compelling the President of India, or Governor of any State, to exercise or refrain from exercising in any manner any of the lawful powers of such President or Governor, assaults or wrongfully restrains, or attempts wrongfully to restrain, or overawes, by means of criminal force or the show of criminal force, or attempts so to overawe, such President or Governor, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Assaulting President, Governor, etc., with intent to compel or restrain exercise of any lawful power
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 124 'Assaulting President, Governor, etc., with intent to compel or restrain the exercise of any lawful power' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 151 'Assaulting President, Governor, etc., with intent to compel or restrain exercise of any lawful power' under CHAPTER VII OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE STATE.

sections.t: Sedition
sections.b: Whoever by words, either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representation, or otherwise, brings or attempts to bring into hatred or contempt, or excites or attempts to excite disaffection towards, the Government established by law in India, a shall be punished with imprisonment for life, to which fine may be added, or with imprisonment which may extend to three years, to which fine may be added, or with fine.

x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 124A 'Sedition' has been repealed and deleted in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

sections.t: Waging war against any Asiatic Power in alliance with the Government of India
sections.b: Whoever wages war against the Government of any Asiatic Power in alliance or at peace with the Government of India or attempts to wage such war, or abets the waging of such war, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, to which fine may be added, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, to which fine may be added, or with fine.

x.targetTitle: Waging war against Government of any foreign State at peace with Government of India
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 125 'Waging war against any Asiatic Power in alliance with the Government of India' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 153 'Waging war against Government of any foreign State at peace with Government of India' under CHAPTER VII OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE STATE.

sections.t: Committing depredation on territories of Power at peace with the Government of India
sections.b: Whoever commits depredation, or makes preparations to commit depredation, on the territories of any Power in alliance or at peace with the Government of India, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine and to forfeiture of any property used or intended to be used in committing such depredation, or acquired by such depredation.

x.targetTitle: Committing depredation on territories of foreign State at peace with Government of India
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 126 'Committing depredation on territories of Power at peace with the Government of India' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 154 'Committing depredation on territories of foreign State at peace with Government of India' under CHAPTER VII OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE STATE.

sections.t: Receiving property taken by war or depredation mentioned in sections 125 and 126
sections.b: Whoever receives any property knowing the same to have been taken in the commission of any of the offences mentioned in sections 125 and 126, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine and to forfeiture of the property so received.

x.targetTitle: Receiving property taken by war or depredation mentioned in sections 153 and 154
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 127 'Receiving property taken by war or depredation mentioned in sections 125 and 126' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 155 'Receiving property taken by war or depredation mentioned in sections 153 and 154' under CHAPTER VII OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE STATE.

sections.t: Public servant voluntarily allowing prisoner of state or war to escape
sections.b: Whoever, being a public servant and having the custody of any State prisoner or prisoner of war, voluntarily allows such prisoner to escape from any place in which such prisoner is confined, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Public servant voluntarily allowing prisoner of State or war to escape
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 128 'Public servant voluntarily allowing prisoner of state or war to escape' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 156 'Public servant voluntarily allowing prisoner of State or war to escape' under CHAPTER VII OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE STATE.

sections.t: Public servant negligently suffering such prisoner to escape
sections.b: Whoever, being a public servant and having the custody of any State prisoner or prisoner of war, negligently suffers such prisoner to escape from any place of confinement in which such prisoner is confined, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Public servant negligently suffering such prisoner to escape
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 129 'Public servant negligently suffering such prisoner to escape' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 157 'Public servant negligently suffering such prisoner to escape' under CHAPTER VII OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE STATE.

sections.t: Aiding escape of, rescuing or harbouring such prisoner
sections.b: Whoever knowingly aids or assists any State prisoner or prisoner of war in escaping from lawful custody, or rescues or attempts to rescue any such prisoner, or harbours or conceals any such prisoner who has escaped from lawful custody, or offers or attempts to offer any resistance to the recapture of such prisoner shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Aiding escape of, rescuing or harbouring such prisoner
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 130 'Aiding escape of, rescuing or harbouring such prisoner' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 158 'Aiding escape of, rescuing or harbouring such prisoner' under CHAPTER VII OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE STATE.

sections.t: Abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from his duty
sections.ct: offences relating to the army, navy and air force
sections.b: Whoever abets the committing of mutiny by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India or attempts to seduce any such officer, soldier, sailor or airman from his allegiance or his duty, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from his duty
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 131 'Abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from his duty' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 159 'Abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from his duty' under CHAPTER VIII OF OFFENCES RELATING TO THE ARMY, NAVY AND AIR FORCE.

sections.t: Abetment of mutiny, if mutiny is committed in consequence thereof
sections.ct: offences relating to the army, navy and air force
sections.b: Whoever abets the committing of mutiny by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India, shall, if mutiny be committed in consequence of that abetment, be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Abetment of mutiny, if mutiny is committed in consequence thereof
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 132 'Abetment of mutiny, if mutiny is committed in consequence thereof' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 160 'Abetment of mutiny, if mutiny is committed in consequence thereof' under CHAPTER VIII OF OFFENCES RELATING TO THE ARMY, NAVY AND AIR FORCE.

sections.t: Abetment of assault by soldier, sailor or airman on his superior officer, when in execution of his office
sections.ct: offences relating to the army, navy and air force
sections.b: Whoever abets an assault by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India, on any superior officer being in the execution of his office, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Abetment of assault by soldier, sailor or airman on his superior officer, when in execution of his office
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 133 'Abetment of assault by soldier, sailor or airman on his superior officer, when in execution of his office' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 161 'Abetment of assault by soldier, sailor or airman on his superior officer, when in execution of his office' under CHAPTER VIII OF OFFENCES RELATING TO THE ARMY, NAVY AND AIR FORCE.

sections.t: Abetment of such assault, if the assault committed
sections.ct: offences relating to the army, navy and air force
sections.b: Whoever abets an assault by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India, on any superior officer being in the execution of his office, shall, if such assault be committed in consequence of that abetment be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Abetment of such assault, if assault committed
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 134 'Abetment of such assault, if the assault committed' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 162 'Abetment of such assault, if assault committed' under CHAPTER VIII OF OFFENCES RELATING TO THE ARMY, NAVY AND AIR FORCE.

sections.t: Abetment of desertion of soldier, sailor or airman
sections.ct: offences relating to the army, navy and air force
sections.b: Whoever, abets the desertion of any officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Abetment of desertion of soldier, sailor or airman
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 135 'Abetment of desertion of soldier, sailor or airman' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 163 'Abetment of desertion of soldier, sailor or airman' under CHAPTER VIII OF OFFENCES RELATING TO THE ARMY, NAVY AND AIR FORCE.

sections.t: Harbouring deserter
sections.ct: offences relating to the army, navy and air force
sections.b: Whoever, except as hereinafter excepted, knowing or having reason to believe that an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India, has deserted, harbours such officer, soldier, sailor or airman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine or with both.

x.targetTitle: Harbouring deserter
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 136 'Harbouring deserter' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 164 'Harbouring deserter' under CHAPTER VIII OF OFFENCES RELATING TO THE ARMY, NAVY AND AIR FORCE.

sections.t: Deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master
sections.ct: offences relating to the army, navy and air force
sections.b: The master or person in charge of a merchant vessel, on board of which any deserter from the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India is concealed, shall, though ignorant of such concealment, be liable to a penalty not exceeding five hundred rupees, if he might have known of such concealment but for some neglect of his duty as such master or person in charge, or but for some want of discipline on board of the vessel.

x.targetTitle: Deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 137 'Deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 165 'Deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master' under CHAPTER VIII OF OFFENCES RELATING TO THE ARMY, NAVY AND AIR FORCE with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Abetment of act of insubordination by soldier, sailor or airman
sections.ct: offences relating to the army, navy and air force
sections.b: Whoever abets what he knows to be an act of insubordination by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or air Force, of the Government of India, shall, if such act of insubordination be committed in consequence of that abetment, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Abetment of act of insubordination by soldier, sailor or airman
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 138 'Abetment of act of insubordination by soldier, sailor or airman' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 166 'Abetment of act of insubordination by soldier, sailor or airman' under CHAPTER VIII OF OFFENCES RELATING TO THE ARMY, NAVY AND AIR FORCE with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Application of foregoing sections to the Indian Marine Service.
sections.ct: offences relating to the army, navy and air force
sections.b: Repealed by the Amending Act, 1934 (35 of 1934), S. 2 and Sch.

sections.t: Persons subject to certain Acts
sections.ct: offences relating to the army, navy and air force
sections.b: No person subject to the Army Act, the Army Act, 1950 (46 of 1950), the Naval Discipline Act, the Indian Navy (Discipline) Act, 1934 (34 of 1934), the Air Force Act or the Air Force Act, 1950 (45 of 1950), is subject to punishment under this Code for any of the offences defined in this Chapter.

x.targetTitle: Persons subject to certain Acts
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 139 'Persons subject to certain Acts' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 167 'Persons subject to certain Acts' under CHAPTER VIII OF OFFENCES RELATING TO THE ARMY, NAVY AND AIR FORCE.

sections.t: Wearing garb or carrying token used by soldier, sailor or airman
sections.ct: offences relating to the army, navy and air force
sections.b: Whoever, not being a soldier, sailor or airman in the Military, Naval or Air service of the Government of India, wears any garb or carries any token resembling any garb or token used by such a soldier, sailor or airman with the intention that it may be believed that he is such a soldier, sailor or airman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Wearing garb or carrying token used by soldier, sailor or airman
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 140 'Wearing garb or carrying token used by soldier, sailor or airman' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 168 'Wearing garb or carrying token used by soldier, sailor or airman' under CHAPTER VIII OF OFFENCES RELATING TO THE ARMY, NAVY AND AIR FORCE with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Unlawful assembly
sections.b: An assembly of five or more persons is designated an “unlawful assembly”, if the common object of the persons composing that assembly is:

x.targetTitle: Unlawful assembly
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 141 'Unlawful assembly' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 189(1) 'Unlawful assembly' under CHAPTER XI OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE PUBLIC TRANQUILLITY.

sections.t: Being member of unlawful assembly
sections.b: Whoever, being aware of facts which render any assembly an unlawful assembly, intentionally joins that assembly, or continues in it, is said to be a member of an unlawful assembly.

x.targetTitle: Unlawful assembly
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 142 'Being member of unlawful assembly' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 189(2) 'Unlawful assembly' under CHAPTER XI OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE PUBLIC TRANQUILLITY.

sections.t: Punishment
sections.b: Whoever is a member of an unlawful assembly, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Unlawful assembly
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 143 'Punishment for unlawful assembly' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 189(2) 'Unlawful assembly' under CHAPTER XI OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE PUBLIC TRANQUILLITY.

sections.t: Joining unlawful assembly armed with deadly weapon
sections.b: Whoever, being armed with any deadly weapon, or with anything which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death, is a member of an unlawful assembly, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Unlawful assembly
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 144 'Joining unlawful assembly armed with deadly weapon' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 189(4) 'Unlawful assembly' under CHAPTER XI OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE PUBLIC TRANQUILLITY.

sections.t: Joining or continuing in unlawful assembly, knowing it has been commanded to disperse
sections.b: Whoever joins or continues in an unlawful assembly, knowing that such unlawful assembly has been commanded in the manner prescribed by law to disperse, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extent to two years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Unlawful assembly
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 145 'Joining or continuing in unlawful assembly, knowing it has been commanded to disperse' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 189(3) 'Unlawful assembly' under CHAPTER XI OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE PUBLIC TRANQUILLITY.

sections.t: Rioting
sections.b: Whenever force or violence is used by an unlawful assembly, or by any member thereof, in prosecution of the common object of such assembly, every member of such assembly is guilty of the offence of rioting.

x.targetTitle: Rioting
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 146 'Rioting' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 191(1) 'Rioting' under CHAPTER XI OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE PUBLIC TRANQUILLITY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Punishment for rioting
sections.b: Whoever is guilty of rioting, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Rioting
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 147 'Punishment for rioting' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 191(2) 'Rioting' under CHAPTER XI OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE PUBLIC TRANQUILLITY.

sections.t: Rioting, armed with deadly weapon
sections.b: Whoever is guilty of rioting, being armed with a deadly weapon or with anything which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Rioting
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 148 'Rioting, armed with deadly weapon' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 191(3) 'Rioting' under CHAPTER XI OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE PUBLIC TRANQUILLITY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object
sections.b: If an offence is committed by any member of an unlawful assembly in prosecution of the common object of that assembly, or such as the members of that assembly knew to be likely to be committed in prosecution of that object, every person who, at the time of the committing of that offence, is a member of the same assembly, is guilty of that offence.

x.targetTitle: Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 149 'Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 190 'Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object' under CHAPTER XI OF OFFENCES AGAINST THE PUBLIC TRANQUILLITY.

sections.t: Hiring, or conniving at hiring, of persons to join unlawful assembly
sections.b: Whoever hires or engages, or employees, or promotes, or connives at the hiring, engagement or employment of any person to join or become a member of any unlawful assembly, shall be punishable as a member of such unlawful assembly, and for any offence which may be committed by any such person as a member of such unlawful assembly in pursuance of such hiring, engagement or employment, in the same manner as if he had been a member of such unlawful assembly, or himself had committed such offence.

sections.t: Knowingly joining or continuing in assembly of five or more persons after it has been commanded to disperse
sections.b: Whoever knowingly joins or continues in any assembly of five or more persons likely to cause a disturbance of the public peace, after such assembly has been lawfully commanded to disperse, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

sections.t: Assaulting or obstructing public servant when suppressing riot, etc.
sections.b: Whoever assaults or threatens to assault, or obstructs or attempts to obstruct, any public servant in the discharge of his duty as such public servant, in endeavouring to disperse an unlawful assembly, or to suppress a riot or affray, or uses, or threatens, or attempts to use criminal force to such public servant, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

sections.t: Wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause riot
sections.b: Whoever malignantly, or wantonly by doing anything which is illegal, gives provocation to any person intending or knowing it to be likely that such provocation will cause the offence of rioting to be committed, shall, if the offence of rioting be committed in consequence of such provocation, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both, and if the offence of rioting be not committed, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

sections.t: Promoting enmity between different groups on ground of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, etc., and doing acts prejudicial to maintenance of harmony
sections.b:
Whoever
by words, either spoken or written, or by signs or by visible representations or otherwise, promotes or attempts to promote, on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or community or any other ground whatsoever, disharmony or feelings of enmity, hatred or ill-will between different religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, or
commits any act which is prejudicial to the maintenance of harmony between different religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, and which disturbs or is likely to disturb the public tranquillity, or
organizes any exercise, movement, drill or other similar activity intending that the participants in such activity shall use or be trained to use criminal force or violence or knowing it to be likely that the participants in such activity will use or be trained to use criminal force or violence, or participates in such activity intending to use or be trained to use criminal force or violence or knowing it to be likely that the participants in such activity will use or be trained to use criminal force or violence, against any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community and such activity for any reason whatsoever causes or is likely to cause fear or alarm or a feeling of insecurity amongst members of such religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
Offence committed in place of worship, etc   Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (1) in any place of worship or in any assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine.

sections.t: Punishment for knowingly carrying arms in any procession or organising or holding or taking part in any mass drill or mass training with arms
sections.b: Whoever knowingly carries arms in any procession or organizes or holds or takes part in any mass drill or mass training with arms in any public place in contravention of any public notice or order issued or made under section 144A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months and with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees.

sections.t: Imputations, assertions prejudicial to national integration
sections.b:
Whoever, by words either spoken or written or by signs or by visible representations or otherwise:
makes or publishes any imputation that any class of persons cannot, by reason of their being members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established or uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India, or
asserts, counsels, advises, propagates or publishes that any class of persons by reason of their being members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community be denied, or deprived of their rights as citizens of India, or
makes or publishes and assertion, counsel, plea or appeal concerning the obligation of any class of persons, by reason of their being members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, and such assertion, counsel, plea or appeal causes or is likely to cause disharmony or feelings of enmity or hatred or ill-will between such members and other persons, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (1), in any place of worship or in any assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine.

sections.t: Owner or occupier of land on which an unlawful assembly is held
sections.b: Whenever any unlawful assembly or riot takes place, the owner or occupier of the land upon which such unlawful assembly is held, or such riot is committed, and any person having or claiming an interest in such land, shall be punishable with fine not exceeding one thousand rupees, if he or his agent or manager, knowing that such offence is being or has been committed, or having reason to believe it is likely to be committed, do not give the earliest notice thereof in his or their power to the principal officer at the nearest police-station, and do not, in the case of his or their having reason to believe that it was about to be committed, use all lawful means in his or their power to prevent it and, in the event of its taking place, do not use all lawful means in his or their power to disperse or suppress the riot or unlawful assembly.

sections.t: Liability of person for whose benefit riot is committed
sections.b: Whenever a riot is committed for the benefit or on behalf of any person who is the owner or occupier of any land respecting which such riot takes place or who claims any interest in such land, or in the subject of any dispute which gave rise to the riot, or who has accepted or derived any benefit therefrom, such person shall be punishable with fine, if he or his agent or manager, having reason to believe that such riot was likely to be committed or that the unlawful assembly by which such riot was committed was likely to be held, shall not respectively use all lawful means in his or their power to prevent such assembly or riot from taking place, and for suppressing and dispersing the same.

sections.t: Public servant disobeying law, with intent to cause injury to any person
sections.ct: offences by or relating to public servants

sections.t: Public Servant disobeying direction under Law
sections.ct: offences by or relating to public servants
sections.b:
Whoever, being a public servant : knowingly disobeys any direction of the law which prohibits him from requiring the attendance at any place of any person for the purpose of investigation into an offence or any other, or knowingly disobeys, to the prejudice of any person, any other direction of the law regulating the manner in which he shall conduct such investigation, or

sections.t: Candidate ,  Electoral right  defined
sections.b:
“candidate” means a person who has been nominated as a candidate at any election;
“electoral right” means the right of a person to stand, or not to stand as, or to withdraw from being, a candidate or to vote or refrain from voting at an election.
