sections.b: If any person under eighteen years of age, any insane person, any delirious person, any idiot, or any person in a state of intoxication commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Abetment of suicide of child or person of unsound mind
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 305 'Abetment of suicide of child or insane person' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 107 'Abetment of suicide of child or person of unsound mind' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY.

sections.t: Abetment of suicide
sections.b: If any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Abetment of suicide
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 306 'Abetment of suicide' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 108 'Abetment of suicide' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY.

sections.t: Attempt to murder
sections.b: Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and, if hurt is caused to any person by such act, the offender shall be liable either to imprisonment for life, or to such punishment as is hereinbefore mentioned.

x.targetTitle: Attempt to murder
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 307 'Attempt to murder' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 109 'Attempt to murder' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Attempt to commit culpable homicide
sections.b: Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and, if hurt is caused to any person by such act, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Attempt to commit culpable homicide
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 308 'Attempt to commit culpable homicide' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 110 'Attempt to commit culpable homicide' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY.

sections.t: Attempt to commit suicide
sections.b: Whoever attempts to commit suicide and does any act towards the commission of such offence, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine, or with both.

x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 309 'Attempt to commit suicide' has been repealed and deleted in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

sections.t: Thug
sections.b: Whoever, at any time after the passing of this Act, shall have been habitually associated with any other or others for the purpose of committing robbery or child-stealing by means of or accompanied with murder, is a thug.

x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 310 'Thug' has been repealed and deleted in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

sections.t: Punishment
sections.b: Whoever is a thug, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 311 'Punishment' has been repealed and deleted in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

sections.t: Causing miscarriage
sections.ct: the causing  miscarriage,  injuries to unborn children,  the exposure  infants, and  the concealment  births
sections.b: Whoever voluntarily causes a woman with child to miscarry, shall if such miscarriage be not caused in good faith for the purpose of saving the life of the woman, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and, if the woman be quick with child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Causing miscarriage
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 312 'Causing miscarriage' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 88 'Causing miscarriage' under CHAPTER V OF OFFENCES AGAINST WOMAN AND CHILD.

sections.t: Causing miscarriage without woman's consent
sections.ct: the causing  miscarriage,  injuries to unborn children,  the exposure  infants, and  the concealment  births
sections.b: Whoever commits the offence defined in the last preceding section without the consent of the woman, whether the woman is quick with child or not, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Causing miscarriage without woman's consent
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 313 'Causing miscarriage without woman's consent' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 89 'Causing miscarriage without woman's consent' under CHAPTER V OF OFFENCES AGAINST WOMAN AND CHILD.

sections.t: Death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage
sections.ct: the causing  miscarriage,  injuries to unborn children,  the exposure  infants, and  the concealment  births
sections.b: Whoever, with intent to cause the miscarriage of a woman with child, does any act which causes the death of such woman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine;

x.targetTitle: Death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 314 'Death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 90 'Death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage' under CHAPTER V OF OFFENCES AGAINST WOMAN AND CHILD.

sections.t: Act done with intent to prevent child being born alive or to cause it to die after birth
sections.ct: the causing  miscarriage,  injuries to unborn children,  the exposure  infants, and  the concealment  births
sections.b: Whoever before the birth of any child does any act with the intention of thereby preventing that child from being born alive or causing it to die after its birth, and does by such act prevent that child from being born alive, or causes it to die after its birth, shall, if such act be not caused in good faith for the purpose of saving the life of the mother, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Act done with intent to prevent child being born alive or to cause to die after birth
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 315 'Act done with intent to prevent child being born alive or to cause it to die after birth' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 91 'Act done with intent to prevent child being born alive or to cause to die after birth' under CHAPTER V OF OFFENCES AGAINST WOMAN AND CHILD.

sections.t: Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide-
sections.ct: the causing  miscarriage,  injuries to unborn children,  the exposure  infants, and  the concealment  births
sections.b: Whoever does any act under such circumstances, that if he thereby caused death he would be guilty of culpable homicide, and does by such act cause the death of a quick unborn child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 316 'Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 92 'Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide' under CHAPTER V OF OFFENCES AGAINST WOMAN AND CHILD.

sections.t: Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years, by parent or person having care of it
sections.ct: the causing  miscarriage,  injuries to unborn children,  the exposure  infants, and  the concealment  births
sections.b: Whoever being the father or mother of a child under the age of twelve years, or having the care of such child, shall expose or leave such child in any place with the intention of wholly abandoning such child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years, by parent or person having care of it
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 317 'Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years, by parent or person having care of it' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 93 'Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years, by parent or person having care of it' under CHAPTER V OF OFFENCES AGAINST WOMAN AND CHILD.

sections.t: Concealment of birth by secret disposal of dead body
sections.ct: the causing  miscarriage,  injuries to unborn children,  the exposure  infants, and  the concealment  births
sections.b: Whoever, by secretly burying or otherwise disposing of the dead body of a child whether such child die before or after or during its birth, intentionally conceals or endeavours to conceal the birth of such child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Concealment of birth by secret disposal of dead body
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 318 'Concealment of birth by secret disposal of dead body' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 94 'Concealment of birth by secret disposal of dead body' under CHAPTER V OF OFFENCES AGAINST WOMAN AND CHILD.

sections.t: Hurt
sections.b: Whoever causes bodily pain, disease or infirmity to any person is said to cause hurt.

x.targetTitle: Hurt
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 319 'Hurt' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 114 'Hurt' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY.

sections.t: Grievous hurt
sections.b:
The following kinds of hurt only are designated as “grievous”: Emasculation.
Permanent privation of the sight of either eye.
Permanent privation of the hearing of either ear.
Privation of any member or joint.
Destruction or permanent impairing of the powers of any member or joint.
Permanent disfiguration of the head or face.
Fracture or dislocation of a bone or tooth.
Any hurt which endangers life or which causes the sufferer to be during the space of twenty days in severe bodily pain, or unable to follow his ordinary pursuits.

x.targetTitle: Grievous hurt
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 320 'Grievous hurt' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 116 'Grievous hurt' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Voluntarily causing hurt
sections.b: Whoever does any act with the intention of thereby causing hurt to any person, or with the knowledge that he is likely thereby to cause hurt to any person, and does thereby cause hurt to any person, is said “voluntarily to cause hurt”.

x.targetTitle: Voluntarily causing hurt
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 321 'Voluntarily causing hurt' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 115(1) 'Voluntarily causing hurt' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt
sections.b: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt, if the hurt which he intends to cause or knows himself to be likely to cause is grievous hurt, and if the hurt which he causes is grievous hurt, is said “voluntarily to cause grievous hurt”.

x.targetTitle: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 322 'Voluntarily causing grievous hurt' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 117(1) 'Voluntarily causing grievous hurt' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Punishment for voluntarily causing hurt
sections.b: Whoever, except in the case provided for by section 334, voluntarily causes hurt, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Voluntarily causing hurt
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 323 'Punishment for voluntarily causing hurt' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 115(2) 'Voluntarily causing hurt' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means
sections.b: Whoever, except in the case provided for by section 334, voluntarily causes hurt by means of any instrument for shooting, stabbing or cutting, or any instrument which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death, or by means of fire or any heated substance, or by means of any poison or any corrosive substance, or by means of any explosive substance or by means of any substance which it is deleterious to the human body to inhale, to swallow, or to receive into the blood, or by means of any animal, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 324 'Voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 118(1) 'Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Punishment for voluntarily causing grievous hurt
sections.b: Whoever, except in the case provided for by section 335, voluntarily causes grievous hurt, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 325 'Punishment for voluntarily causing grievous hurt' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 117(2) 'Voluntarily causing grievous hurt' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY.

sections.t: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means
sections.b: Whoever, except in the case provided for by section 335, voluntarily causes grievous hurt by means of any instrument for shooting, stabbing or cutting, or any instrument which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death, or by means of fire or any heated substance, or by means of any poison or any corrosive substance, or by means of any explosive substance, or by means of any substance which it is deleterious to the human body to inhale, to swallow, or to receive into the blood, or by means of any animal, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 326 'Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 118(2) 'Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid, etc.
sections.b: Whoever causes permanent or partial damage or deformity to, or bums or maims or disfigures or disables, any part or parts of the body of a person or causes grievous hurt by throwing acid1 on or by administering acid to that person, or by using any other means with the intention of causing or with the knowledge that he is likely to cause such injury or hurt, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and with fine;

x.targetTitle: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid, etc
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 326A 'Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid, etc' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 124(1) 'Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid, etc' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY.

sections.t: Voluntarily throwing or attempting to throw acid, etc.
sections.b: Whoever throws or attempts to throw acid1 on any person or attempts to administer acid to any person, or attempts to use any other means, with the intention of causing permanent or partial damage or deformity or bums or maiming or disfigurement or disability or grievous hurt to that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than five years but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid, etc
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 326B 'Voluntarily throwing or attempting to throw acid' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 124(2) 'Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid, etc' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY.

sections.t: Voluntarily causing hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal to an act
sections.b: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt, for the purpose of extorting from the sufferer, or from any person interested in the sufferer, any property or valuable security, or of constraining the sufferer or any person interested in such sufferer to do anything which is illegal or which may facilitate the commission of an offence, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 327 'Voluntarily causing hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal to an act' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 119(1) 'Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY.

sections.t: Causing hurt by means of poison, etc., with intent to commit and offence
sections.b: Whoever administers to or causes to be taken by any person any poison or any stupefying, intoxicating or unwholesome drug, or other thing with intent to cause hurt to such person, or with intent to commit or to facilitate the commission of an offence or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause hurt, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Causing hurt by means of poison, etc., with intent to commit an offence
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 328 'Causing hurt by means of poison, etc., with intent to commit and offence' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 123 'Causing hurt by means of poison, etc., with intent to commit an offence' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY.

sections.t: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act
sections.b: Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt for the purpose of extorting from the sufferer or from any person interested in the sufferer any property or valuable security, or of constraining the sufferer or any person interested in such sufferer to do anything that is illegal or which may facilitate the commission of an offence, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 329 'Voluntarily causing grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 119(2) 'Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY.

sections.t: Voluntarily causing hurt to extort confession or to compel restoration of property
sections.b: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt, for the purpose of extorting from the sufferer or from any person interested in the sufferer, any confession or any information which may lead to the detection of an offence or misconduct, or for the purpose of constraining the sufferer or any person interested in the sufferer to restore or to cause the restoration of any property or valuable security or to satisfy any claim or demand, or to give information which may lead to the restoration of any property or valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 330 'Voluntarily causing hurt to extort confession, or to compel restoration of property' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 120(1) 'Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY.

sections.t: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt to extort confession, or to compel restoration of property
sections.b: Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt for the purpose of extorting from the sufferer or from any person interested in the sufferer any confession or any information which may lead to the detection of an offence or misconduct, or for the purpose of constraining the sufferer or any person interested in the sufferer to restore or to cause the restoration of any property or valuable security, or to satisfy any claim or demand or to give information which may lead to the restoration of any property or valuable security shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 331 'Voluntarily causing grievous hurt to extort confession, or to compel restoration of property' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 120(2) 'Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY.

sections.t: Voluntarily causing hurt to deter public servant from his duty
sections.b: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt to any person being a public servant in the discharge of his duty as such public servant, or with intent to prevent or deter that person or any other public servant from discharging his duty as such public servant, or in consequence of anything done or attempted to be done by that person in the lawful discharge of his duty as such public servant, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 332 'Voluntarily causing hurt to deter public servant from his duty' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 121(1) 'Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty
sections.b: Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt to any person being a public servant in the discharge of his duty as such public servant, or with intent to prevent or deter that person or any other public servant from discharging his duty as such public servant, or in consequence of anything done or attempted to be done by that person in the lawful discharge of his duty as such public servant, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 333 'Voluntarily causing grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 121(2) 'Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Voluntarily causing hurt on provocation
sections.b: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt on grave and sudden provocation, if he neither intends nor knows himself to be likely to cause hurt to any person other than the person who gave the provocation, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt on provocation
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 334 'Voluntarily causing hurt on provocation' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 122(1) 'Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt on provocation' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt on provocation
sections.b: Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt on grave and sudden provocation, if he neither intends nor knows himself to be likely to cause grievous hurt to any person other than the person who gave the provocation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to four years, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt on provocation
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 335 'Voluntarily causing grievous hurt on provocation' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 122(2) 'Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt on provocation' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Act endangering life or personal safety of others
sections.b: Whoever does any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or the personal safety others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to two hundred and fifty rupees, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Act endangering life or personal safety of others
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 336 'Act endangering life or personal safety of others' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 125 'Act endangering life or personal safety of others' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Causing hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others
sections.b: Whoever causes hurt to any person by doing any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Act endangering life or personal safety of others
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 337 'Causing hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 125(a) 'Act endangering life or personal safety of others' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Causing grievous hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others
sections.b: Whoever causes grievous hurt to any person by doing any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Act endangering life or personal safety of others
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 338 'Causing grievous hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 125(b) 'Act endangering life or personal safety of others' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Wrongful restraint
sections.b: Whoever voluntarily obstructs any person so as to prevent that person from proceeding in any direction in which that person has a right to proceed, is said wrongfully to restrain that person.

x.targetTitle: Wrongful restraint
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 339 'Wrongful restraint' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 126(1) 'Wrongful restraint' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Wrongful confinement
sections.b: Whoever wrongfully restrains any person in such a manner as to prevent that person from proceeding beyond certain circumscribing limits, is said “wrongfully to confine” that person.

x.targetTitle: Wrongful confinement
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 340 'Wrongful confinement' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 127(1) 'Wrongful confinement' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Punishment for wrongful restraint
sections.b: Whoever wrongfully restrains any person shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Wrongful restraint
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 341 'Punishment for wrongful restraint' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 126(2) 'Wrongful restraint' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Punishment for wrongful confinement
sections.b: Whoever wrongfully confines any person shall be punished with simple imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Wrongful confinement
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 342 'Punishment for wrongful confinement' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 127(2) 'Wrongful confinement' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Wrongful confinement for three or more days
sections.b: Whoever wrongfully confines any person for three days or more, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Wrongful confinement
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 343 'Wrongful confinement for three or more days' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 127(3) 'Wrongful confinement' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Wrongful confinement for ten or more days
sections.b: Whoever wrongfully confines any person for ten days, or more, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Wrongful confinement
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 344 'Wrongful confinement for ten or more days' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 127(4) 'Wrongful confinement' under CHAPTER VI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Wrongful confinement of person for whose liberation writ has been issued
sections.b: Whoever keeps any person in wrongful confinement, knowing that a writ for the liberation of that person has been duly issued, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years in addition to any term of imprisonment to which he may be liable under any other section of this Chapter.

x.targetTitle: Wrongful confinement

sections.t: Wrongful confinement in secret

sections.t: Trafficking of persons
sections.ct: kidnapping, abduction, slavery and forced labour
sections.b:
Whoever, for the purpose of exploitation, (a) recruits, (b) transports, ( c) harbours, (d) transfers, or (e) receives, a person or persons, by 
using threats, or
using force, or any other form of coercion, or
by abduction, or
by practising fraud, or deception, or
by abuse of power, or
by inducement, including the giving or receiving of payments or benefits, in order to achieve the consent of any person having control over the person recruited, transported, harboured, transferred or received,
commits the offence of trafficking1. Explanations
1. The expression “exploitation” shall include any act of physical exploitation or any form of sexual exploitation, slavery or practices similar to slavery, servitude, or the forced removal of organs.
2. The consent of the victim is immaterial in determination of the offence of trafficking1.
Whoever commits the offence of trafficking shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years, but which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
Where the offence involves the trafficking1 of more than one person, it shall be punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
Where the offence involves the trafficking of a minor, it shall be punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
Where the offence involves the trafficking of more than one minor, it shall be punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than fourteen years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
If a person is convicted of the offence of trafficking of minor on more than one occasion, then such person shall be punished with imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, and shall also be liable to fine.
When a public servant or a police officer is involved in the trafficking of any person then, such public servant or police officer shall be punished with imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, and shall also be liable to fine.

sections.t: Rape
sections.b:
A man is said to commit “rape” if he, penetrates his penis, to any extent, into the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of a woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person; or
inserts, to any extent, any object or a part of the body, not being the penis, into the vagina, the urethra or anus of a woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person; or
manipulates any part of the body of a woman so as to cause penetration into the vagina, urethra, anus or any part of body of such woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person; or
applies his mouth to the vagina, anus, urethra of a woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person, under the circumstances falling under any of the following seven descriptions1:
Against her will.
Without her consent.
With her consent, when her consent has been obtained by putting her or any person in whom she is interested, in fear of death or of hurt.
With her consent, when the man knows that he is not her husband and that her consent is given because she believes that he is another man to whom she is or believes herself to be lawfully married.
With her consent when, at the time of giving such consent, by reason of unsoundness of mind or intoxication or the administration by him personally or through another of any stupefying or unwholesome Substance, she is unable to understand the nature and consequences of that to which she gives consent.
With or without her consent, when she is under eighteen years of age.
When she is unable to communicate consent.
Explanations
For the purposes of this section, “vagina” shall also include labia majora.
Consent means an unequivocal voluntary agreement when the woman by words, gestures or any form of verbal or non-verbal communication, communicates willingness to participate in the specific sexual act;
Provided that a woman who does not physically resist to the act of penetration shall not by the reason only of that fact, be regarded as consenting to the sexual activity.
Exceptions
A medical procedure or intervention shall not constitute rape.
Sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, the wife not being under fifteen years of age, is not rape.

sections.t: Punishment for rape
sections.b:
Whoever, except in the cases provided for in sub-section (2), commits rape, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
Whoever 
being a police officer, commits rape,
within the limits of the police station to which such police officer is appointed; or
in the premises of any station house; or
on a woman in such police officer’s custody or in the custody of a police officer subordinate to such police officer; or
being a public servant, commits rape on a woman in such public servant’s custody or in the custody of a public servant subordinate to such public servant; or
being a member of the armed forces deployed in an area by the Central or a State Government commits rape in such area; or
being on the management or on the staff of a jail, remand home or other place of custody established by or under any law for the time being in force or of a women’s or children’s institution, commits rape on any inmate of such jail, remand home, place or institution; or
being on the management or on the staff of a hospital, commits rape on a woman in that hospital; or
being a relative, guardian or teacher of, or a person in a position of trust or authority towards the woman, commits rape on such woman; or
commits rape during communal or sectarian violence; or
commits rape on a woman knowing her to be pregnant; or
commits rape, on a woman incapable of giving consent; or
being in a position of control or dominance over a woman, commits rape on such woman; or
commits rape on a woman suffering from mental or physical disability; or
while committing rape causes grievous bodily harm or maims or disfigures or endangers the life of a woman; or
commits rape repeatedly on the same woman,
shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, and shall also be liable to fine.
Whoever, commits rape on a woman under sixteen years of age shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, and shall also be liable to fine:1
Provided that such fine shall be just and reasonable to meet the medical expenses and rehabilitation of the victim:
Provided further that any fine imposed under this sub-section shall be paid to the victim.
Explanations
For the purposes of sub-section 2
“armed forces” means the naval, military and air forces and includes any member of the Armed Forces constituted under any Law for the time being in force, including the paramilitary forces and any auxiliary forces that are under the control of the Central Government, or the State Government;
“hospital” means the precincts of the hospital and includes the precincts of any institution for the reception and treatment of persons during convalescence or of persons requiring medical attention or rehabilitation;
“police officer” shall have the same meaning as assigned to the expression “police” under the Police Act, 1861;
“women’s or children’s institution” means an institution, whether called an orphanage or a home for neglected women or children or a widow’s home or an institution called by any other name, which is established and maintained for the reception and care of women or children.

sections.t: Sexual intercourse by person in authority
sections.b:
Whoever, being, in a position of authority or in a fiduciary relationship; or
a public servant; or
superintendent or manager of a jail, remand home or other place of custody established by or under any law for the time being in force, or a women’s or children’s institution; or
on the management of a hospital or being on the staff of a hospital, abuses such position or fiduciary relationship to induce or seduce any woman either in his custody or under his charge or present in the premises to have sexual intercourse with him, such sexual intercourse not amounting to the offence of rape, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than 5 years, but which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine1.
Explanations
In this section, “sexual intercourse” shall mean any of the acts mentioned in clauses (a) to (d) of section 375.
For the purposes of this section, Explanation 1 to section 375 shall also be applicable.
“Superintendent”, in relation to a jail, remand home or other place of custody or a women’s or children’s institution, includes a person holding any other office in such jail, remand home, place or institution by virtue of which such person can exercise any authority or control over its inmates.
The expressions “hospital” and “women’s or children’s institution” shall respectively have the same meaning as in Explanation to sub-section (2) of section 376.

sections.t: Robbery
sections.b: In all robbery there is either theft or extortion. When theft is robbery   Theft is “robbery” if, in order to the committing of the theft, or in committing the theft, or in carrying away or attempting to carry away property obtained by the theft, the offender, for that end, voluntarily causes or attempts to cause to any person death or hurt or wrongful restraint, or fear of instant death or of instant hurt, or of instant wrongful restraint. When extortion is robbery   Extortion is “robbery” if the offender, at the time of committing the extortion, is in the presence of the person put in fear, and commits the extortion by putting that person in fear of instant death, of instant hurt, or of instant wrongful restraint to that person or to some other person, and, by so putting in fear, induces the person, so put in fear then and there to deliver up the thing extorted.

sections.b: Whoever, being a clerk or servant or employed as a clerk or servant, and being in any manner entrusted in such capacity with property, or with any dominion over property, commits criminal breach of trust in respect of that property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Criminal breach of trust
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 408 'Criminal breach of trust by clerk or servant' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 316(4) 'Criminal breach of trust' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Criminal breach of trust by public servant, or by banker, merchant or agent
sections.b: Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property in his capacity of a public servant or in the way of his business as a banker, merchant, factor, broker, attorney or agent, commits criminal breach of trust in respect of that property, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Criminal breach of trust
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 409 'Criminal breach of trust by public servant, or by banker, merchant or agent' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 316(5) 'Criminal breach of trust' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Stolen property
sections.b: Property, the possession whereof has been transferred by theft, or by extortion, or by robbery, and property which has been criminally misappropriated or in respect of which criminal breach of trust has been committed, is designated as “stolen property”, whether the transfer has been made, or the misappropriation or breach of trust has been committed, within or without India. But, if such property subsequently comes into the possession of a person legally entitled to the possession thereof, it then ceases to be stolen property.

x.targetTitle: Stolen property
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 410 'Stolen property' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 317(1) 'Stolen property' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Dishonestly receiving stolen property
sections.b: Whoever dishonestly receives or retains any stolen property, knowing or having reason to believe the same to be stolen property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Stolen property
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 411 'Dishonestly receiving stolen property' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 317(2) 'Stolen property' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Dishonestly receiving property stolen in the commission of a dacoity
sections.b: Whoever dishonestly receives or retains any stolen property, the possession whereof he knows or has reason to believe to have been transferred by the commission of dacoity, or dishonestly receives from a person, whom he knows or has reason to believe to belong or to have belonged to a gang of dacoits, property which he knows or has reason to believe to have been stolen, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Stolen property
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 412 'Dishonestly receiving property stolen in the commission of a dacoity' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 317(3) 'Stolen property' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Habitually dealing in stolen property
sections.b: Whoever habitually receives or deals in property which he knows or has reason to believe to be stolen property, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Stolen property
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 413 'Habitually dealing in stolen property' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 317(4) 'Stolen property' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Assisting in concealment of stolen property
sections.b: Whoever voluntarily assists in concealing or disposing of or making away with property which he knows or has reason to believe to be stolen property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Stolen property
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 414 'Assisting in concealment of stolen property' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 317(5) 'Stolen property' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Cheating
sections.b: Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property, or intentionally induces the person so deceived to do or omit to do anything which he would not do or omit if he were not so deceived, and which act or omission causes or is likely to cause damage or harm to that person in body, mind, reputation or property, is said to “cheat”.

x.targetTitle: Cheating
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 415 'Cheating' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 318(1) 'Cheating' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Cheating by personation
sections.b: A person is said to “cheat by personation” if he cheats by pretending to be some other person, or by knowingly substituting one person for or another, or representing that he or any other person is a person other than he or such other person really is.

x.targetTitle: Cheating by personation
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 416 'Cheating by personation' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 319(1) 'Cheating by personation' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Punishment for cheating
sections.b: Whoever cheats shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Cheating
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 417 'Punishment for cheating' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 318(2) 'Cheating' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Cheating with knowledge that wrongful loss may ensue to person whose interest offender is bound to protect
sections.b: Whoever cheats with the knowledge that he is likely thereby to cause wrongful loss to a person whose interest in the transaction to which the cheating relates, he was bound either by law, or by legal contract, to protect, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Cheating
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 418 'Cheating with knowledge that wrongful loss may ensue to person whose interest offender is bound to protect' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 318(3) 'Cheating' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Punishment for cheating by personation
sections.b: Whoever cheats by personation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Cheating
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 419 'Punishment of cheating by personation' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 319(2) 'Cheating' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
sections.b: Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Cheating
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 420 'Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 318(4) 'Cheating' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent distribution among creditors
sections.b: Whoever dishonestly or fraudulently removes, conceals or delivers to any person, or transfers or causes to be transferred to any person, without adequate consideration, any property, intending thereby to prevent, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby prevent the distribution of that property according to law among his creditors or the creditors of any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent distribution among creditors
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 421 'Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent distribution among creditors' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 320 'Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent distribution among creditors' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Dishonestly or fraudulently preventing debt being available for creditors
sections.b: Whoever dishonestly or fraudulently prevents any debt or demand due to himself or to any other person from being made available according to law for payment of his debts or the debts of such other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Dishonestly or fraudulently preventing debt being available for creditors
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 422 'Dishonestly or fraudulently preventing debt being available for creditors' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 321 'Dishonestly or fraudulently preventing debt being available for creditors' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Dishonest or fraudulent execution of deed of transfer containing false statement of consideration
sections.b: Whoever dishonestly or fraudulently signs, executes or becomes a party to any deed or instrument which purports to transfer or subject to any charge any property, or any interest therein, and which contains any false statement relating to the consideration for such transfer or charge, or relating to the person or persons for whose use or benefit it is really intended to operate, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Dishonest or fraudulent execution of deed of transfer containing false statement of consideration
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 423 'Dishonest or fraudulent execution of deed of transfer containing false statement of consideration' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 322 'Dishonest or fraudulent execution of deed of transfer containing false statement of consideration' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property
sections.b: Whoever dishonestly or fraudulently conceals or removes any property of himself or any other person, or dishonestly or fraudulently assists in the concealment or removal thereof, or dishonestly releases any demand or claim to which he is entitled, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 424 'Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 323 'Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Mischief
sections.b: Whoever with intent to cause, or knowing that he is likely to cause, wrongful loss or damage to the public or to any person, causes the destruction of any property, or any such change in any property or in the situation thereof as destroys or diminishes its value or utility, or affects it injuriously, commits “mischief”.

x.targetTitle: Mischief
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 425 'Mischief' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 324(1) 'Mischief' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Punishment for mischief
sections.b: Whoever commits mischief shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Mischief
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 426 'Punishment for mischief' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 324(2) 'Mischief' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Mischief causing damage to the amount of fifty rupees
sections.b: Whoever commits mischief and thereby causes loss or damage to the amount of fifty rupees or upwards, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Mischief causing damage to the amount of twenty thousand rupees and more but less than one lakh rupees
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 427 'Mischief causing damage to the amount of fifty rupees' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 324(4) 'Mischief causing damage to the amount of twenty thousand rupees and more but less than one lakh rupees' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Mischief by killing or maiming animal of the value of ten rupees
sections.b: Whoever commits mischief by killing, poisoning, maiming or rendering useless any animals or animal of the value of the ten rupees or upwards, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Mischief by killing or maiming animal
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 428 'Mischief by killing or maiming animal of the value of ten rupees' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 325 'Mischief by killing or maiming animal' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Mischief by killing or maiming cattle, etc., of any value or any animal of the value of fifty rupees
sections.b: Whoever commits mischief by killing, poisoning, maiming or rendering useless, any elephant, camel, horse, mule, buffalo, bull, cow or ox, whatever may be the value thereof, of any other animal of the value of fifty rupees or upwards, shall be punished with imprisonment or either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Mischief by killing or maiming animal
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 429 'Mischief by killing or maiming cattle, etc., of any value or any animal of the value of fifty rupees' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 325 'Mischief by killing or maiming animal' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Mischief by injury to works of irrigation or by wrongfully diverting water
sections.b: Whoever commits mischief by doing any act which causes, or which he knows to be likely to cause, a diminution of the supply of water for agricultural purposes, or for food or drink for human beings or for animals which are property, or for cleanliness or for carrying on any manufacture, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 430 'Mischief by injury to works of irrigation or by wrongfully diverting water' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 326(a) 'Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Mischief by injury to public road, bridge, river or channel
sections.b: Whoever commits mischief by doing any act which renders or which he knows to be likely to render any public road, bridge, navigable river or navigable channel, natural or artificial, impassable or less safe for travelling or conveying property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 431 'Mischief by injury to public road, bridge, river or channel' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 326(b) 'Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Mischief by causing inundation or obstruction to public drainage attended with damage
sections.b: Whoever commits mischief by doing any act which causes or which he knows to be likely to cause an inundation or an obstruction to any public drainage attended with injury or damage, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 432 'Mischief by causing inundation or obstruction to public drainage attended with damage' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 326(c) 'Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Mischief by destroying, moving or rendering less useful a light-house or sea-mark
sections.b: Whoever commits mischief by destroying or moving any light-house or other light used as a sea-mark, or any sea-mark or buoy or other thing placed as a guide for navigators, or by any act which renders any such light-house, sea-mark, buoy or other such thing as aforesaid less useful as a guide for navigators, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 433 'Mischief by destroying, moving or rendering less useful a light-house or sea-mark' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 326(d) 'Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Mischief by destroying or moving, etc., a land-mark fixed by public authority
sections.b: Whoever commits mischief by destroying or moving any land-mark fixed by the authority of a public servant, or by any act which renders such land-mark less useful as such, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 434 'Mischief by destroying or moving, etc., a land-mark fixed by public authority' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 326(e) 'Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Mischief by fire or explosive substance with intent to cause damage to amount of one hundred or (in case of agricultural produce) ten rupees
sections.b: Whoever commits mischief by fire or any explosive substance intending to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, damage to any property to the amount of one hundred rupees or upwards or (where the property is agricultural produce) ten rupees or upwards, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 435 'Mischief by fire or explosive substance with intent to cause damage to amount of one hundred or (in case of agricultural produce) ten rupees' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 326(f) 'Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Mischief by fire or explosive substance with intent destroy house, etc.
sections.b: Whoever commits mischief by fire or any explosive substance, intending to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause the destruction of any building which is ordinarily used as a place of worship or as a human dwelling or as a place for the custody of property, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 436 'Mischief by fire or explosive substance with intent to destroy house, etc' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 326(g) 'Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Mischief with intent to destroy or make unsafe a decked vessel or one of twenty tons burden
sections.b: Whoever commits mischief to any decked vessel or any vessel of a burden of twenty tons or upwards, intending to destroy or render unsafe, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby destroy or render unsafe, that vessel, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Mischief with intent to destroy or make unsafe a rail, aircraft, decked vessel or one of twenty tons burden
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 437 'Mischief with intent to destroy or make unsafe a decked vessel or one of twenty tons burden' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 327(1) 'Mischief with intent to destroy or make unsafe a rail, aircraft, decked vessel or one of twenty tons burden' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Punishment for the mischief described in section 437 committed by fire or explosive substance
sections.b: Whoever commits, or attempts to commit, by fire or any explosive substance, such mischief as is described in the last preceding section. shall be punished with imprisonment for life. or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Mischief with intent to destroy or make unsafe a rail, aircraft, decked vessel or one of twenty tons burden
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 438 'Punishment for the mischief described in section 437 committed by fire or explosive substance' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 327(2) 'Mischief with intent to destroy or make unsafe a rail, aircraft, decked vessel or one of twenty tons burden' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Punishment for intentionally running vessel aground or ashore with intent to commit theft, etc.
sections.b: Whoever intentionally runs any vessel aground or ashore, intending to commit theft of any property contained therein or to dishonestly misappropriate any such property, or with intent that such theft or misappropriation of property may be committed, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Punishment for intentionally running vessel aground or ashore with intent to commit theft, etc
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 439 'Punishment for intentionally running vessel aground or ashore with intent to commit theft, etc' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 328 'Punishment for intentionally running vessel aground or ashore with intent to commit theft, etc' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Mischief committed after preparation made for causing death or hurt
sections.b: Whoever commits mischief, having made preparation for causing to any person death, or hurt, or wrongful restraint, or fear of death, or hurt, or of wrongful restraint, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Mischief
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 440 'Mischief committed after preparation made for causing death or hurt' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 324(6) 'Mischief' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Criminal trespass
sections.b: Whoever enters into or upon property in the possession of another with intent to commit an offence or to intimidate, insult or annoy any person in possession of such property, or having lawfully entered into or upon such property, unlawfully remains there with intent thereby to intimidate, insult or annoy any such person, or with intent to commit an offence, is said to commit “criminal trespass”.

x.targetTitle: Criminal trespass and house-trespass
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 441 'Criminal trespass' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 329(1) 'Criminal trespass and house-trespass' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: House-trespass
sections.b: Whoever commits criminal trespass by entering into or remaining in any building, tent or vessel used as a human dwelling or any building used as a place for worship, or as a place for the custody of property, is said to commit “house-trespass”.

x.targetTitle: Criminal trespass and house-trespass
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 442 'House-trespass' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 329(2) 'Criminal trespass and house-trespass' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Lurking house-trespass
sections.b: Whoever commits house-trespass having taken precautions to conceal such house-trespass from some person who has a right to exclude or eject the trespasser from the building, tent or vessel which is the subject of the trespass, is said to commit “lurking house-trespass”.

x.targetTitle: House-trespass and house-breaking
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 443 'Lurking house-trespass' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 330(1) 'House-trespass and house-breaking' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Lurking house-trespass by night
sections.b: Whoever commits lurking house-trespass after sunset and before sunrise, is said to commit “lurking house-trespass by night”.

x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 444 'Lurking house-trespass by night' has been repealed and deleted in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

sections.t: House-breaking
sections.b: A person is said to commit “house-breaking” who commits house-trespass if he effects his entrance into the house or any part of it in any of the six ways hereinafter described;

x.targetTitle: House-trespass and house-breaking
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 445 'House-breaking' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 330(2) 'House-trespass and house-breaking' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: House-breaking by night
sections.b: Whoever commits house-breaking after sunset and before sunrise, is said to commit “house-breaking by night”.

x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 446 'House-breaking by night' has been repealed and deleted in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

sections.t: Punishment for criminal trespass
sections.b: Whoever commits criminal trespass shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Criminal trespass and house-trespass
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 447 'Punishment for criminal trespass' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 329(3) 'Criminal trespass and house-trespass' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: Punishment for house-trespass
sections.b: Whoever commits house-trespass shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

x.targetTitle: Criminal trespass and house-trespass
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 448 'Punishment for house-trespass' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 329(4) 'Criminal trespass and house-trespass' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY with amendments (Change).

sections.t: House-trespass in order to commit offence punishable with death
sections.b: Whoever commits house-trespass in order to the committing of any offence punishable with death, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: House-trespass in order to commit offence
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 449 'House-trespass in order to commit offence punishable with death' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 332(a) 'House-trespass in order to commit offence' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: House-trespass in order to commit offence punishable with imprisonment for life
sections.b: Whoever commits house-trespass in order to the committing of any offence punishable with imprisonment for life, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: House-trespass in order to commit offence
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 450 'House-trespass in order to commit offence punishable with imprisonment for life' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 332(b) 'House-trespass in order to commit offence' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: House-trespass in order to commit offence punishable with imprisonment
sections.b: Whoever commits house-trespass in order to the committing of any offence punishable with imprisonment, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, and shall also be liable to fine;

x.targetTitle: House-trespass in order to commit offence
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 451 'House-trespass in order to commit offence punishable with imprisonment' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 332(c) 'House-trespass in order to commit offence' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: House-trespass after preparation for hurt, assault or wrongful restraint
sections.b: Whoever commits house-trespass, having made preparation for causing hurt to any person or for assaulting any person, or for wrongfully restraining any person, or for putting and person in fear of hurt, or of assault, or of wrongful restraint, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: House-trespass after preparation for hurt, assault or wrongful restraint
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 452 'House-trespass after preparation for hurt, assault or wrongful restraint' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 333 'House-trespass after preparation for hurt, assault or wrongful restraint' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Punishment for lurking house-trespass or house-breaking
sections.b: Whoever commits lurking house-trespass or house-breaking, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, and shall also be liable to fine.

x.targetTitle: Punishment for house-trespass or house-breaking
x.note: Indian Penal Code, 1860 Section 453 'Punishment for lurking house-trespass or house-breaking' corresponds to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 Section 331(1) 'Punishment for house-trespass or house-breaking' under CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY.

sections.t: Lurking house-trespass or house-breaking in order to commit offence punishable with imprisonment
sections.b: Whoever commits lurking house-trespass or house-breaking, in order to the committing of any offence punishable with imprisonment, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine;

sections.t: Grievous hurt caused whilst committing lurking house-trespass or house-breaking
sections.b: Whoever, whilst committing lurking house-trespass or house-breaking, causes grievous hurt to any person or attempts to cause death or grievous hurt to any person, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

sections.t: All persons jointly concerned in lurking house-trespass or house-breaking by night punishable where death or grievous hurt caused by one of them
sections.b: If at the time of the committing of lurking house-trespass by night or house-breaking by night, any person guilty of such offence shall voluntarily cause or attempt to cause death or grievous hurt to any person, every person jointly concerned in committing such lurking house-trespass by night or house-breaking by night, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

sections.t: Dishonestly breaking open receptacle containing property
sections.b: Whoever dishonestly or with intent to commit mischief, breaks open or unfastens any closed receptacle which contains or which he believes to contain property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

sections.t: Punishment for same offence when committed by person entrusted with custody
sections.b: Whoever, being entrusted with any closed receptacle which contains or which he believes to contain property without having authority to open the same, dishonestly, or with intent to commit mischief, breaks open or unfastens that receptacle, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

sections.t: Forgery
sections.ct: offences relating to documents and to property marks
sections.b: Whoever makes any false document or false electronic record or part of a document or electronic record with intent to cause damage or injury, to the public or to any person, or to support any claim or title, or to cause any person to part with property, or to enter into any express or implied contract, or with intent to commit fraud or that fraud may be committed, commits forgery.

sections.t: Punishment for forgery
sections.ct: offences relating to documents and to property marks
sections.b: Whoever commits forgery shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
